templates.pattern: Read the information and answer: [P1] is the son of [P2]. [P2] is the daughter of [P3]. [P3] is the husband of [P4]. [P4] is the daughter of [P5]. [P5] is the wife of [P6]. How is [P6] related to [P1]?
templates.explanation: [P2] is mother of [P1]. [P3] is father of [P2] = maternal grandfather of [P1]. [P4] is mother of [P2] (wife of [P3]) = maternal grandmother of [P1]. [P5] is mother of [P4]. [P6] is father of [P4] = [P1]'s maternal great-grandfather.

templates.pattern: In a coded language: 'A$B' means A is the mother of B, 'A@B' means A is the husband of B, 'A#B' means A is the brother of B, 'A%B' means A is the daughter of B. If [P1]$[P2]@[P3]#[P4]%[P5], how is [P5] related to [P1]?
templates.explanation: [P1]$[P2]: [P1] is mother of [P2]. [P2]@[P3]: [P2] is husband of [P3] → [P3] is wife/daughter-in-law of [P1]. [P3]#[P4]: [P3] is brother of [P4]. [P4]%[P5]: [P4] is daughter of [P5]. [P5] is parent of [P4] who is sibling of [P3] = parent of [P3]'s sibling. [P5] is Father/Mother-in-law of [P2] = [P1]'s in-law's parent.

templates.pattern: Six members of a family: [P1],[P2],[P3],[P4],[P5],[P6]. [P1] and [P2] are married. [P1] is the father of [P3] and [P4]. [P3] is married to [P5]. [P5] is the sister of [P6]. [P6] is the son of [P2]'s sister. How is [P6] related to [P4]?
templates.explanation: [P5] married [P3] = [P4]'s sibling. [P6] is brother of [P5] = brother-in-law of [P3] = [P4]'s sibling's brother-in-law. [P6] is also cousin of [P3]/[P4] through [P2]'s sister's son. [P6] is Cousin of [P4].

templates.pattern: Pointing to a girl, [P1] said, 'She is the daughter of the only son of my grandmother.' How is the girl related to [P1]?
templates.explanation: My grandmother's only son = my father. Daughter of my father = my sister. The girl is [P1]'s Sister.

templates.pattern: If [P1] is [P2]'s brother, [P3] is [P2]'s mother, [P4] is [P3]'s father, [P5] is [P4]'s mother, and [P5] has only one grandchild [P6], how is [P6] related to [P2]?
templates.explanation: [P5] is great-grandmother of [P2] (through [P4]->[P3]->[P2]). [P5]'s only grandchild = [P3]. [P6] = grandchild of [P5] = [P3]. But [P3] is mother of [P2]. So [P6] = [P3] = [P2]'s Mother.

templates.pattern: Study the information: [P1] has two children. [P2] is the spouse of [P1]. [P3] is the son-in-law of [P2]. [P4] is the granddaughter of [P1]. [P4] has no siblings. [P5] is the daughter of [P1]. How is [P3] related to [P5]?
templates.explanation: [P3] is son-in-law of [P2] = married to a child of [P1]/[P2]. [P5] is daughter. So [P3] is Husband of [P5].

templates.pattern: In a family: 'P→Q' means P is the parent of Q. 'P↔Q' means P and Q are siblings. 'P⇒Q' means P is married to Q. Given: [P1]→[P2], [P2]↔[P3], [P3]⇒[P4], [P4]→[P5], [P5]↔[P6]. How is [P6] related to [P1]?
templates.explanation: [P1] is parent of [P2]. [P2] and [P3] are siblings → [P3] is also child of [P1]. [P3] married [P4]. [P4] is parent of [P5] and [P6]. [P6] is grandchild of [P1] through [P3].

templates.pattern: [P1] told [P2]: 'The lady whose photo you saw is my mother's only brother's wife's only daughter's husband's mother.' How is that lady related to [P1]?
templates.explanation: Mother's only brother = maternal uncle. Uncle's wife = maternal aunt. Aunt's only daughter = cousin. Cousin's husband's mother = cousin's mother-in-law. No standard term = Cousin's mother-in-law.

templates.pattern: In a family of 7: [P1] is grandfather. [P2] is grandmother. [P3] is their son. [P4] is [P3]'s wife. [P5] and [P6] are children of [P3]. [P7] is the spouse of [P5]. [P7]'s father is [P8]. How is [P8] related to [P1]?
templates.explanation: [P7] is spouse of [P5] = grandchild-in-law of [P1]. [P8] is father of [P7] = Co-parent-in-law of [P1]'s son.

templates.pattern: Using the code where '+' = son, '-' = daughter, '×' = father, '÷' = mother: If [P1]+[P2]-[P3]×[P4]÷[P5], how is [P5] related to [P1]?
templates.explanation: [P1]+[P2]: [P2] is son of [P1]. [P2]-[P3]: [P3] is daughter of [P2]. [P3]×[P4]: [P4] is father of [P3]. [P4]÷[P5]: [P5] is mother of [P4]. [P5] is mother of [P4] = grandmother of [P3] = great-grandmother of [P1]'s grandson = [P1]'s grandson's mother's mother = [P1]'s great-grandchild's ancestor. Chain: [P1]→[P2]→[P3]←[P4]←[P5]. [P5] is [P4]'s mother and [P4] is [P3]'s father and [P3] is [P2]'s daughter and [P2] is [P1]'s son. [P5] is Mother of [P1]'s granddaughter's father.

templates.pattern: [P1] is the maternal uncle of [P2]. [P2] is the brother of [P3]. [P3]'s mother is [P4]. [P4]'s husband is [P5]. [P5] is the son of [P6]. How is [P6] related to [P1]?
templates.explanation: [P1] is maternal uncle of [P2] → [P1] is brother of [P4] (mother of [P2]/[P3]). [P5] is husband of [P4]. [P6] is father of [P5] = father-in-law of [P4] = father-in-law of [P1]'s sister.

templates.pattern: In a group photograph, [P1] says 'From left, first is my uncle. Second is my uncle's wife. Third is my cousin. Fourth is that cousin's son. Fifth is me.' The 4th person is how related to the 2nd person?
templates.explanation: 2nd = uncle's wife. 3rd = cousin = uncle's wife's child. 4th = cousin's son = uncle's wife's grandson. 4th person is Grandson of 2nd person.

templates.pattern: Given: [P1] is the brother of [P2]'s mother. [P3] is the father of [P2]. [P4] is the sister of [P3]. [P5] is the mother of [P4]'s only son. How is [P5] related to [P1]?
templates.explanation: [P1] is maternal uncle of [P2]. [P3] is father of [P2]. [P4] is sister of [P3] = paternal aunt of [P2]. [P5] is mother of [P4]'s only son = [P4]'s daughter-in-law. No direct relation to [P1]. [P5] is unrelated by blood to [P1].

templates.pattern: A woman introduces a man saying 'His wife is the only daughter of my mother's mother.' How is the woman related to the man?
templates.explanation: My mother's mother = maternal grandmother. Only daughter of grandmother = my mother. Man's wife = the woman's mother. So the woman is the man's Daughter.

templates.pattern: Five persons [P1]-[P5] are in a family. [P1] is the father of [P2] and [P3]. [P4] is the wife of [P2]. [P5] is the son of [P3]. [P4]'s mother-in-law's husband's son's son is [P5]. Verify and find how [P5] is related to [P4].
templates.explanation: [P4]'s mother-in-law = [P1]'s wife (mother of [P2]). Husband = [P1]. [P1]'s son = [P2] or [P3]. [P3]'s son = [P5]. So [P5] is Nephew of [P4] (son of husband's brother).

templates.pattern: In a family tree, [P1] has two sons [P2] and [P3]. [P2] has a daughter [P4]. [P3] has a son [P5]. [P4] marries [P5]. They have a son [P6]. How is [P6] related to [P1]?
templates.explanation: [P4] and [P5] are cousins (both grandchildren of [P1]). [P6] is their son = great-grandchild of [P1].

templates.pattern: Decode: '!' means father, '!!' means mother, '@' means brother, '@@' means sister, '&' means son, '&&' means daughter. [P1]![P2]@@[P3]&&[P4]@[P5]. How is [P5] related to [P1]?
templates.explanation: [P1]![P2]: [P1] is father of [P2]. [P2]@@[P3]: [P2] is sister of [P3] → siblings. [P3]&&[P4]: [P3] is daughter of [P4]? No — '&&' means daughter, so [P3] is daughter? Reread: [P3]&&[P4] means [P3] is daughter of [P4]. Wait — the format is A symbol B meaning A [relation] B. So [P3]&&[P4]: [P3] is daughter of [P4] → [P4] is parent of [P3] = [P1]'s child's parent = [P1]'s child's other parent = [P1]'s spouse context. [P4]@[P5]: [P4] is brother of [P5]. [P5] is sibling of [P4] who is parent of [P3] who is sibling of [P2] who is child of [P1]. [P5] is [P1]'s daughter-in-law's co-parent = no standard term. Simplified: [P5] is [P4]'s sibling = [P3]'s parent's sibling. [P5] is Uncle/Aunt of [P3] = Uncle/Aunt of [P1]'s grandchild-through-[P2].

templates.pattern: Read carefully: [P1] and [P2] are brothers. [P3] is the wife of [P1]. [P4] is the only child of [P2]. [P5] is the son of [P3]. [P5] and [P4] are best friends. How is [P4] related to [P3]?
templates.explanation: [P3] is wife of [P1]. [P2] is brother of [P1]. [P4] is child of [P2] = nephew/niece of [P1] = nephew/niece of [P3] (by marriage). [P4] is Nephew/Niece of [P3].

templates.pattern: In a UPSC-style puzzle: M is the son of N. O is the brother of P. P is the daughter of N. Q is the father of M. R is the mother of O. How is R related to N?
templates.explanation: N is parent of M and P. Q is father of M = Q is N's spouse (if N is mother) or Q=N. M is son of N. Q is father of M → Q is husband of N (N is mother). O is brother of P → O is also child of N. R is mother of O → R is mother of N's child → R is N herself or N's co-parent. R = N (mother of O who is N's child). R is N herself. R is the Same Person as N.

templates.pattern: [P1] is the son of [P2]'s mother's brother. [P3] is the daughter of [P2]. [P4] is the husband of [P3]. [P5] is the son of [P4]. How is [P5] related to [P1]?
templates.explanation: [P1] is cousin of [P2] (son of [P2]'s maternal uncle). [P3] is [P2]'s daughter. [P5] is [P3]'s son = [P2]'s grandson. [P1] is [P2]'s cousin. [P5] is [P2]'s grandson. [P5] is Cousin's nephew (no standard term). [P5] is [P1]'s cousin's grandson.

templates.pattern: In a family: [P1] has three children: [P2] (son), [P3] (daughter), [P4] (son). [P3] is married to [P5]. [P5]'s brother is [P6]. [P6]'s daughter is [P7]. How is [P7] related to [P2]?
templates.explanation: [P3] married [P5]. [P6] is brother of [P5] = brother-in-law of [P3] = [P2]'s sibling's brother-in-law. [P7] is daughter of [P6]. No standard term between [P7] and [P2]. [P7] is [P2]'s sister's brother-in-law's daughter.

templates.pattern: A is married to B. C is the son of A. D is the sister of C. E is the mother-in-law of B. F is the brother of E. G is the daughter of F. How is G related to D?
templates.explanation: A married B. C and D are children of A. E is mother-in-law of B = mother of A. F is brother of E = uncle of A. G is daughter of F = cousin of A = cousin of C and D. G is Cousin of D.

templates.pattern: If [P1] says '[P2] is my father's brother's son's daughter', and [P3] says '[P2] is my mother's sister's son's daughter', what relation do [P1] and [P3] share (through [P2])?
templates.explanation: [P2] is [P1]'s cousin's daughter = [P1]'s second cousin. [P2] is [P3]'s cousin's daughter = [P3]'s second cousin. Both [P1] and [P3] are second cousins of [P2]. [P1] and [P3] are Co-second-cousins.

templates.pattern: In a UPSC puzzle: P, Q, R, S, T are five family members. P is the father of Q and R. S is the wife of Q. T is the son of R. S's mother-in-law is T's grandmother. True or False?
templates.explanation: P is father of Q and R. S is wife of Q → S's mother-in-law = P's wife (Q's mother). T is son of R → T's grandmother = P's wife. S's mother-in-law = T's grandmother = P's wife. TRUE.

templates.pattern: Read the passage: [P1] has two daughters [P2] and [P3]. [P2] is married to [P4]. [P4] has a sister [P5]. [P5] has a son [P6]. [P6]'s grandmother on his father's side is [P7]. How is [P7] related to [P1]?
templates.explanation: [P4] and [P5] are siblings. [P7] is paternal grandmother of [P6] = mother of [P6]'s father. [P6] is son of [P5]. [P6]'s father = [P5]'s husband. [P7] is mother of [P5]'s husband = [P4]'s mother (if same family) = mother-in-law of [P2]. [P7] is [P2]'s mother-in-law = [P1]'s daughter's mother-in-law.
